correctness.rationale: The pinned source defines a unit flow on a finite acyclic directed graph with every arc on a source-sink route and at least two distinct routes. Nonnegative flow decomposes into route-incidence vectors because of acyclicity. Arc precedence e<f when head(e) reaches tail(f) is a strict poset, and a chain of arcs extends to a route. Dilworth makes its width w equal the minimum number of routes covering all arcs, allowing overlaps. For an admissible reflection with factor lambda every c_e>=1/(lambda+1); summing over a size-w antichain yields lambda>=w-1 since a route meets an antichain at most once. Averaging a width-w route cover gives a unit flow c_e>=1/w; for any c with those inequalities, wc-chi_R is a nonnegative flow of strength w-1 for every route R, yielding exact containment for all F(G), and conversely this condition is forced at optimum. Positive integer flows decompose into integer routes, so the minimal k with all arc entries positive is exactly cover width w; this is the codegree in the declared lattice. A matching in the transitive-closure poset provides w=|E|-nu. No inference from the bounded checker is necessary for the all-DAG proof.
residual_risks: The program enumerates finitely many small DAGs, not every DAG; was read but not executed independently this run.
Directed cycles, inaccessible arcs and capacitated/different-demand flow systems are not in this theorem.

value.rationale: Acyclic unit-flow polytopes are central combinatorial optimization objects, and Minkowski asymmetry is a natural but difficult affine invariant. Identifying it exactly for arbitrary acyclic networks by a readily computable arc-poset width, simultaneously classifying every center and relating the same number to lattice codegree, is a genuine complete infinite-family structural classification. The polytime Dilworth matching formula is useful even when the graph is not planar, balanced, or Gorenstein.
residual_risks: Value does not rest on 1,393 finite test graphs; the theorem and center-locus relation supply the motivation.

limitations: Finite acyclic DAG, all arcs route-supported, at least two distinct routes; unit total strength, natural relative lattice.
Directed cycles, general demands, capacities, and singleton route polytopes excluded.
